newsitem.title: UK: Chile's Garcia sees rate cut, defends price target.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Garcia sees rate cut, defends price target.

text.p: Chile's economy minister said on Monday he saw interest rates easing within the next six months and defended his country's 1997 inflation target against criticism it was overly ambitious.
"Our purpose is to slow down economic growth and that's already happening," Alvaro Garcia told Reuters in an interview in London.

"We feel we have to keep on slowing down the economy until it reaches about the 6.0 percent level. When that is done, we'll bring interest rates down. I would expect that that will happen within the next six months," he said during a four-day official visit to Britain.
"As soon as it happens the adjustment process will be over," he said.
Since last year the Chilean government has used a policy of high interest rates to slow the economy, which had appeared in danger of overheating.
Financial markets are now hoping the central bank and the ministry of finance will agree to bring rates down soon, fearing the policy will slow growth too sharply.
Chile's Central Bank President Carlos Massad said earlier that rates would not come down until the bank was convinced it would safely meet its growth and inflation targets.
"We're on our way to meeting those targets for 1996, and we don't want to risk not meeting those targets," he said.
The government has targeted 7.0 percent GDP growth in 1996 and 5.5 percent to 6.0 percent growth in 1997. Its inflation goal centres on 6.5 percent this year, falling to 5.5 percent in 1997.
Some Latin American analysts have criticised the inflation target as too difficult to achieve, but Garcia said he was confident it was attainable.
"For six years in a row now the government has reached its inflationary target every single year," he said.

"The market thought the inflation target this year was particularly ambitious because of the increase in the price of major imports in Chile, such as oil and wheat. But annualised, we already have an inflation rate of 6.3 percent today," he said.
"I don't think that the inflation target is overly ambitious for next year," the minister said.
Chile presented its 1997 budget to congress late last month and is awaiting its approval.
Garcia said the budget called for a 10 percent increase in spending on education and health while maintaining a fiscal surplus of 2.0 percent of GDP.
Regarding privatisation, he said only the water companies were left to be sold by the government.

"I would expect the process to be completed by next year....We're in the last stages of legislating on that matter. As soon as that happens, we start privatising, and there's nothing else left beside the copper company."
But he ruled out selling off the jewel in the Chilean crown, state copper company Codelco.
"This government won't move ahead on privatising existing copper companies," he said, adding Codelco would not be privatised during the present government's term in office.
